requirements.statement: A condition-passing MSR takes either Rm or the ARM rotated immediate as its operand, expands the four field bits to byte masks, and writes the selected CPSR or current-mode SPSR fields. A failed condition has no architectural effect.
The immediate MSR operand is the zero-extended 8-bit immediate rotated right by twice rotate_imm; all 4096 encoded immediates obey the same PSR update restrictions as register operands.

User-mode CPSR writes affect only user-writable flags; privileged/state fields are ignored. SPSR access without a current SPSR, a privileged CPSR attempt to select T state, an operand setting any unallocated bit, or a selected control field receiving a reserved mode encoding is UNPREDICTABLE and produces no constrained PSR-write intent.
ARMv4T MSR treats PSR bits[27:8] as unallocated, permits User writes only to NZCV, and permits privileged CPSR control writes to I, F, and M[4:0] while excluding T.

source_refs.locator: §A4.1.39 Table A4-1, operation, usage example, and T-bit note

requirements.notes: Issue I prints PrivMask as 0x0000000F, but its normative usage says MSR updates interrupt enables and its example sets CPSR bit 7 through CPSR_c. The implemented 0x000000DF restores those explicitly required I/F bits and excludes StateMask bit 5.
